papers.title: Continuous Policy and Value Iteration for Stochastic Control Problems and Its Convergence
papers.publication_status: arXiv preprint; v2 revised in 2026; no journal reference verified
papers.fulltext_read_definition: 取得整篇全文，实际阅读以下正文段落及关键公式/定理/算法；并非逐页通读全部附录或独立复证。

read_scope.not_read: Other convergence branches and most proofs/appendices are not fully read.

assumptions: Controlled drift AND diffusion; bounded C2 coefficients, uniformly elliptic covariance and discounted value regularity (Assumption 2).
Convergence requires monotonicity of value/gradient/Hessian dynamics (Assumption 28); Proposition 30 adds curvature and uniform derivative bounds.
guarantees_reported: Authors derive continuous policy/value iteration and contraction of value derivatives; under extra curvature hypotheses policy laws converge in Wasserstein distance.
limits: Learning time τ differs from physical time t; their Langevin Brownian motion differs from plant Brownian motion.
Policy-averaged diffusion is sqrt(Eπ[σσᵀ]), not Eπ[σ].
Ideal functional/PDE dynamics are not a guarantee for a finite-feature MATLAB actor-critic; finite-horizon extension explicitly not direct (§6.1).

Separate physical_dt, actor_update_dt, iteration_time; randomized-policy density/entropy/reference measure optional.

papers.publication_status: Accepted to Human-aligned RL workshop at ICRA 2024 according to arXiv; not verified as main-track ICRA paper
papers.fulltext_read_definition: 取得整篇全文，实际阅读以下正文段落及关键公式/定理/算法；并非逐页通读全部附录或独立复证。

read_scope.not_read: Full experiments and complete proof audit not performed; model-error limitation in conclusion inspected.

assumptions: Continuous deterministic ODE sampled under zero-order hold; stochastic actor is not physical diffusion.
DT CBF constraints use predicted states, and CLF learning relies on expected Lyapunov decrease.
guarantees_reported: Proposes primary actor and safety backup actor, performance critics, Lyapunov critic, learned NODE, and augmented-Lagrangian CLF/CBF actor updates.
limits: Sampled/minibatch expectation constraints on a learned model do not themselves establish real-system statewise safety.
Paper notes NODE discrepancy can be unknown/large; backup activation depends on task configuration.

Keep SAC/NODE implementation as optional backend, not base MATLAB dependency.

papers.title: Mean field LQG social optimization: A reinforcement learning approach
papers.publication_status: Published in Automatica; author manuscript read
papers.fulltext_read_definition: 取得整篇全文，实际阅读以下正文段落及关键公式/定理/算法；并非逐页通读全部附录或独立复证。

read_scope.not_read: Remaining numerical section and every detailed proof not independently re-derived.

assumptions: Homogeneous linear agents with independent scalar Brownian noise; multiplicative diffusion Cx+Du.
Mean-square stabilizability, exact observability, initial-state moment/independence conditions and a stabilizing initial gain.
Two full-rank data conditions; expectation regressors approximated using repeated trajectories.
guarantees_reported: Off-policy PI learns stochastic Riccati and mean-field gains; policy is asymptotically decentralized social-optimal as population grows under stated assumptions.
limits: Social team optimum is different from Nash equilibrium.
Finite Monte Carlo approximation and finite population are separate errors; exact expectation/rank theorems do not automatically bound finite-run errors.
Mean of xxᵀ differs from product of mean x; control-dependent diffusion changes the quadratic greedy matrix to R+DᵀPD.

papers.title: Ergodic-risk Criterion for Stochastically Stabilizing Policy Optimization
papers.publication_status: arXiv preprint v3; no journal/accepted conference reference verified
papers.fulltext_read_definition: 取得整篇全文，实际阅读以下正文段落及关键公式/定理/算法；并非逐页通读全部附录或独立复证。

read_scope.not_read: Intervening general Markov-chain limit-theorem proofs and full simulations not read exhaustively.

assumptions: DT linear system; stabilizability, iid zero-mean noise, controllability and finite fourth moment for quadratic-risk limiting variance.
Strong duality/algorithm specialize to state-only risk Rc=0 and linear policy offset ell=0; Q positive and noise channel full-row rank; Slater condition.
guarantees_reported: Defines long-run risk using conditional-variance limit of centered cumulative risk and gives primal-dual average-cost LQR synthesis under restricted conditions.
limits: This is not discounted expected cost, exponential utility, CVaR of a total return, or worst-case H∞.
Algorithm has model-based gradient/Lyapunov-oracle access; finite-sample data-driven sample complexity is explicitly left to readers.
Finite fourth moment is still a substantive assumption; heavy-tailed does not mean arbitrary heavy tails.

papers.title: Independent RL for Cooperative-Competitive Agents: A Mean-Field Perspective
papers.publication_status: arXiv preprint v2; formal venue not verified
papers.fulltext_read_definition: 取得整篇全文，实际阅读以下正文段落及关键公式/定理/算法；并非逐页通读全部附录或独立复证。

read_scope.not_read: Long appendices, including sample-path oracle extension in Appendix J, not fully read.

assumptions: Finite-horizon DT LQ teams with intra-team cooperation and inter-team general-sum competition; both common and idiosyncratic Gaussian noise.
Equilibrium requires coupled matrix invertibility; independent NPG convergence requires diagonal dominance, controlled gradient errors and step sizes.
Main algorithm uses expected perturbed cost oracle and chosen initial covariance; sample-path extension is separate appendix.
guarantees_reported: Authors characterize mean-field-type Nash policy and O(1/min team size) finite-population epsilon-Nash approximation; MRNPG converges under stated conditions.
limits: Independent parameter updates do not imply arbitrary neighbor-only sensor/communication topology.
Policies use joint generic state and conditional population mean; mean is conditioned on common noise.
The game assumptions are LQ/finite horizon and are not generic nonlinear MARL guarantees.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Policy and Lyapunov-Certificate Learning
papers.publication_status: Published in IEEE Open Journal of Control Systems; accepted author manuscript read
papers.venue: IEEE Open Journal of Control Systems 3 (2024), 375–388
papers.fulltext_read_definition: 取得整篇全文，实际阅读以下正文段落及关键公式/定理/算法；并非逐页通读全部附录或独立复证。

read_scope.not_read: Numerical comparison section and all proofs not independently revalidated.

visual_verification.focus: Eq.(30) aggregation placement and Proposition VI.5 claim/proof

assumptions: ODE f(x,u)+W(x,u)ξ; uncertain parameter ξ remains fixed over time (Remark V.5), compact state/action/parameter sets.
Wasserstein ambiguity set around uncertainty samples; finite-sample confidence radius depends on tail/constants.
Neural certificate theorem requires zero empirical loss, sufficiently dense state covering and Lipschitz/derivative bounds outside a delta ball.
guarantees_reported: Uniform-over-domain distributionally robust chance condition yields a probability statement for fixed-parameter systems; neural result gives delta-accurate stabilization.
limits: Random fixed parameter is not Brownian diffusion or temporally resampled disturbance.
Pointwise alternative loss (40) has global stability analysis explicitly deferred (Remark VI.7).
Positive training loss does not meet the zero-loss theorem; compact domain and delta-neighborhood must be retained in claims.

Potential formula-to-proof gap requiring independent audit: printed Eq.(30) aggregates the sum over state samples before positive-part; Proposition VI.5 proof infers per-state constraints from zero aggregate loss. Cancellation can invalidate that inference without an extra assumption or modified loss. PDF page 8 visually verified; not a full-paper invalidity finding.

code.scope: Exact paper hyperlink opened; repository and README confirm paper, DR_LF_Learning, environment and examples. Not executed, not theorem-to-code audited.

module_action: Add UncertaintySpec mode=fixed_parameter_distribution, samples, support, Wasserstein order/radius, confidence and trajectory persistence.
CertificateSpec records uniform_vs_pointwise, risk epsilon, sample confidence epsilon_bar, delta ball, verification domain and method.
Keep learned performance value and Lyapunov certificate distinct; optional external neural verifier adapter.
Do not accept zero aggregate training loss as certification. Independently evaluate each sample/domain residual and audit loss-to-theorem implication before reuse.

papers.title: Action Gaps and Advantages in Continuous-Time Distributional Reinforcement Learning
papers.publication_status: Published in NeurIPS 2024 proceedings; arXiv author fulltext read
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (NeurIPS 2024)
papers.fulltext_read_definition: 取得整篇全文，实际阅读以下正文段落及关键公式/定理/算法；并非逐页通读全部附录或独立复证。

read_scope.not_read: Full appendix proofs, Algorithm 2/3 details and trading experiment not read exhaustively.

assumptions: Controlled SDE and relaxed-policy averaged covariance; Lipschitz/linear-growth assumptions, with additional reward/terminal regularity for rate results.
Action-independent reward in this paper; discrete action comparisons and quantile representations.
guarantees_reported: Quantifies return-distribution collapse at high decision frequency; quantile-coupled superiority and h^(1/2) scaling preserve distributional action gaps under conditions; risk-greedy ranking result for distortion measures.
limits: Return-distribution modeling differs from distributionally robust model uncertainty.
Risk-distorted action ranking is not a Lyapunov/CBF safety theorem.
q=1/2 preserves distributional scaling while mean advantage requires another scale; changing dt cannot simply reuse fixed-gamma Q targets.

code.scope: Exact PDF hyperlink opened; repository describes author DSUP(q) implementation for NeurIPS 2024. No code execution or reproduction.

gap: Value/Q representation is scalar-only and timing fields do not currently bind return-law scaling and risk functional.
module_action: Optional distributional-return extension: value_representation=quantiles, risk_functional, action_persistence_h, physical discount and superiority scaling.
Core contract stores integration interval and converts physical discount consistently; DSUP/deep network dependency stays optional.
